ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit PEP database, the United Nations Consolidated List (UNSCR 1267, 1373, 1988), the OFAC SDN List, the UK Sanctions List, and New Zealand domestic sanctions lists under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and United Nations Sanctions Act 1988; any PEP match or adverse media trigger requires enhanced due diligence and escalation to a designated AML/CFT compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use the Latin alphabet, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation; names in English and Māori are acceptable; no mandatory transliteration is required, but names must be readable and compliant with the Registrar's naming conventions; non-Latin scripts require separate ministerial or registrar approval and are not generally accepted for standard pre-incorporation clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (unless part of the actual statutory suffix)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Registrar must provide reasons; the applicant may correct and resubmit a new name application, or contest the refusal by filing a written objection with the Companies Office within 20 working days of the rejection notice; unresolved objections may be pursued through administrative review under the Companies Act 1993 and ultimately by judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for a low-risk gaming anti-cheat middleware company subject to the condition that a real physical street address in New Zealand is maintained as the registered office for service of process and statutory correspondence; the virtual office provider must be an approved registered office service provider.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated <5% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a standard low-risk ISIC 6201 non-licensed business, absent adverse screening results, suspicious transaction reports, or regulatory complaints.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (NZ), Part 2 (Incorporation), Part 3 (Constitution and Name), Part 6 (Share Capital and Issue of Shares), Part 7 (Registered Office and Records), Part 8 (Directors), and Schedule 1 (Default Constitution); Financial Reporting Act 2013 for reporting obligations; Income Tax Act 2007 for tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Application for Registration of a New Zealand Company (Companies Office electronic form via the MBIE Companies Register portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Companies Act 1993. A New Zealand company may be incorporated with one or more shares having no par value; subscribers may agree to pay nominal or zero consideration. No statutory escrow account is required, but any subscription funds received must be held by the directors and applied in accordance with the first board resolution and the company's constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the Company), made on [DATE] under the Companies Act 1993.

1. Constitution. RESOLVED that the proposed constitution is adopted, subject to the mandatory provisions of the Companies Act 1993, and that filing with the Registrar be authorized.

2. Registered office. RESOLVED that the registered office is set at [physical street address], New Zealand, and that any change be notified to the Companies Office.

3. Share capital. RESOLVED that [subscriber] subscribe for [number] ordinary shares at NZ$[amount] per share, that the consideration be [cash/non-cash], and that the shares be allotted and entered in the share register.

4. Officers. RESOLVED that [A] and [B] be appointed directors, that [A] be chairperson, and that [C] be appointed corporate secretary with authority to open and operate bank accounts and payment service provider arrangements, including SWIFT wire and Stripe.

5. General authority. RESOLVED that all lawful acts required for registration, licensing, and commencement of the anti-cheat engine business be taken by the directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and proposed constitution approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE (online name search and reservation portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Register. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and must not contain restricted words unless prior approval is obtained. Submit the proposed constitution or expressly adopt the default rules in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993. Ensure director consents and proof of identity are prepared for the next filing step.
required_dossiers: Proposed constitution or Schedule 1 adoption statement
Directors' certified identity documents and residential address evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the name, respond with an online correction and any required written consents or certificates. If the name is declined, amend the proposed name and resubmit within 10 working days; if a third party objects, file a formal objection response with the Companies Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the online incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies through the Companies Office Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office Online portal and complete the electronic Application for Registration of a Company. Enter the company name, registered office street address in New Zealand, director particulars, share structure and subscriber details, and pay the applicable filing fee. Declare compliance with the Companies Act 1993 and authorise the Registrar to register the company.
required_dossiers: Directors' full legal names, residential addresses, and dates of birth
Proof of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for missing or inconsistent data, use the portal to amend and resubmit the affected pages within the prescribed response period. If the Registrar issues a formal refusal, provide corrected annexures and request administrative review; a further appeal may be made by judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration, certificate of incorporation, and NZBN issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon verification of the application, the Registrar will register the company, allocate a company number and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), and issue an electronic Certificate of Incorporation. Download the certificate and company extract from the Companies Register, verify the statutory details, and place the original electronic documents in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated due to a portal or processing error, contact the Companies Office service desk with the application reference number. If registration is refused, request written reasons, cure the identified defect, and re-file; if necessary, seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of registered office and corporate governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and registered office provider; notified to the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical street address in New Zealand suitable for service of documents, not solely a post office box. Open and maintain the company register, share register, register of directors, and minute book. Record the first board resolutions and all share allotments. If the registered office changes, file the prescribed notice with the Companies Office within the statutory timeframe.
required_dossiers: Evidence of registered office address (lease or service agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a non-compliance notice for records or service address, hold an emergency board meeting to ratify the records and file the necessary rectification forms. A substantial defect may be cured by applying for an administrative correction under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, payroll, and workplace compliance activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), WorkSafe New Zealand, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and local territorial authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company's IRD number and register for applicable taxes, including PAYE for employee remuneration. Review Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 obligations for the software development office, confirm workplace ergonomics and display screen equipment standards, arrange a fire safety evacuation scheme if required, and ensure the premises hold a building warrant of fitness or equivalent occupancy certification.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and officer appointment record
IRD registration application (IR596 or online equivalent)
Fire safety and building warrant documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD or WorkSafe raises a query, immediately file corrected registrations or a workplace compliance declaration. If an infringement notice is issued, engage legal counsel and seek abatement or an amendment under the applicable compliance procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure software and middleware business under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511. If a physical hardware manufacturing or data-center facility is later established, the competent authority would be the local territorial authority and MBIE Building and Tenancy Services for building and industrial process approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating license is mandated for video game kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware in New Zealand. The company must still comply with general privacy, data security, and financial services regulations where applicable, such as the Privacy Act 2020 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for office-based software development and middleware engineering activities under the Resource Management Act 1991; no Full EIA Report or Registration Certificate is required for this scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste discharge is generated by software code development and hosting arrangements. If cooled server rooms or physical data-center hardware are installed, comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality, covered Stormwater Management, and the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the business premises: obtain or verify fire safety certification and an evacuation scheme under the Fire Safety and Evacuation Procedures Regulations 2018 administered by Fire and Emergency New Zealand; secure a building warrant of fitness for the leased commercial space; and comply with WorkSafe New Zealand health and safety duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including workstation ergonomics and PPE-free software development activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tauhake) – New Zealand Inland Revenue; official online portal: myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (CK_IC) first obtains an IRD number for tax purposes. For GST registration, the company files Form IR356 (Registration for Goods and Services Tax) via myIR or paper; a non-resident without a place of business in New Zealand must appoint an NZ-resident agent and file a written appointment together with the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office address, director details, and a description of the taxable activity. For an IRD number without GST, the company files Form IR596 (Non-resident Company IRD Number Application) supported by the certificate of incorporation and evidence of the non-resident status. A non-resident IC that has no New Zealand permanent establishment and derives no New Zealand-sourced income is not required to file NZ income tax returns; however, GST registration becomes mandatory from 1 April 2025 for non-resident suppliers of remote services (including gaming anti-cheat middleware) supplied to New Zealand consumers, irrespective of turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope; Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident classification) – the CK_IC is liable to NZ tax only on New Zealand-sourced income under ss YD 4 and YD 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007; offshore business profits, software licensing royalties, and anti-cheat middleware licence fees derived from non-resident customers are outside the NZ tax base and effectively exempt, provided no NZ permanent establishment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections relevant to an International Company: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election for closely held NZ-resident companies (generally unavailable to a non-resident IC); (2) branch exemption election for foreign PEs under s DNHS of the Income Tax Act 2007; (3) optional GST registration election for non-residents making supplies below the statutory threshold; (4) attribution election for offshore portfolio share investments under the FDR rules; (5) hybrid mismatch provisions under subpart FH are mandatory and override any elective treatment, with no elective opt-out; and (6) a deemed-residence election for a company incorporated outside NZ is not permitted where head office and central management remain in the Cook Islands or other offshore jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – a destination-based value-added tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand over any 12-month period for domestic goods and services; from 1 April 2025, non-resident suppliers of remote services (imported digital services, including gaming anti-cheat middleware and SaaS) have a nil registration threshold and must register for GST regardless of turnover; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold for suppliers with a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand. Inland Revenue requires GST returns and relevant schedules to be filed electronically via myIR. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol network, with phased B2G e-invoicing mandates planned but not yet operative. Tax invoices must comply with s 24 of the GST Act 1985, include the supplier's IRD/GST registration number, the date, description, quantity, and amount of consideration, and be issued within 28 days of supply. No government pre-clearance or API-based clearance of invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% GST where they are physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier or delivered to a carrier for export within 28 days of the supply, or supplied to a non-resident who exports the goods. Services qualify for 0% GST when supplied to a non-resident outside New Zealand and the services are not physically performed in New Zealand, or when supplied to a GST-registered resident business for its taxable activity (B2B zero-rating). Gaming anti-cheat middleware supplied by way of software licence, SaaS, or integrity security services to non-resident gaming operators qualifies for zero-rating where the place of supply is offshore and the benefit is consumed outside New Zealand. The supplier must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence of export, non-residence, and offshore consumption at the time the return is filed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (ECMS/Tradelink), including the exporter code and Customs Entry Number
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing loading at a New Zealand port/airport and delivery to a foreign destination
Commercial Invoice and packing list identifying the exported goods, software deliverables or hardware, and the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank advice evidencing full settlement of export proceeds in foreign currency
Signed contract or licence agreement for the gaming anti-cheat engine confirming the foreign counterparty, place of supply, and offshore consumption
Certificate of Non-Residence or IRD letter confirming the supplier's status for zero-rating of services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are scrutinised by Inland Revenue under s 11 of the GST Act 1985. Where export documentation is defective, the supply is recharacterised as a domestic supply, or the recipient is found to be a New Zealand resident, the 15% GST is assessed as a tax shortfall together with use-of-money interest (prescribed rate ~8.14% per annum) and shortfall penalties escalate by culpability: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion, with criminal prosecution available. Wrongly refunded GST is clawed back retrospectively, refund claims are subject to a 4-year statutory time bar, and directors of the International Company may incur personal liability for GST debts under s 149 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current and capital account convertibility under its statutory framework and is an IMF Article VIII member. There are no exchange-control restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, interest, royalties, loan repayments, or equity injection proceeds. The New Zealand dollar is freely floating and may be purchased or sold onshore and offshore without exchange-control approval; the only relevant compliance gate is the AML/CFT and sanctions assessment performed by the receiving bank. Foreign investment screening applies only to sensitive assets under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which is not applicable to the conduct of a software anti-cheat middleware business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline within which export receipts must be repatriated. An International Company may receive foreign-currency service fees for ISIC 6201 anti-cheat software and retain those proceeds in a New Zealand foreign-currency account or an approved offshore account, convert them at market rates, or apply them directly to outbound trade disbursements without prior Reserve Bank approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, subject to clear legal constraints. New Zealand does not issue an offshore digital EMI licence. A non-bank provider must be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and must comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. An offshore EMI may provide multi-currency transaction processing, cards, and FX conversion, but it cannot independently access New Zealand's local retail clearing rails and will require a sponsor bank. For a tax-exempt International Company, an offshore EMI is acceptable for operational disbursements and subscription collections, but it must be supported by a principal New Zealand bank account for escrow, settling, and documentary trade transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, a physical branch visit of every director is not a statutory requirement; banks may use certified electronic identity verification, non-face-to-face CDD, and video-conference interviews where risk is managed. In practice, leading New Zealand banks require at least one authorised director, or a formally appointed signatory, to attend an in-person or high-grade video interview before onboarding a non-resident International Company with no New Zealand operational footprint. A purely remote onboarding is possible only where the bank accepts verified digital identity evidence and the beneficial-ownership documentation is complete and transparent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company with no New Zealand operational substance and no local tax registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation or registration extract, current memorandum and articles, board resolutions appointing directors and authorising bank account opening, register of directors and shareholders, beneficial ownership diagram, business plan evidencing the ISIC 6201 gaming anti-cheat middleware commercial model, and audited financial statements or an accountant-confirmed opening balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain involving a foreign trust or nominee shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deed or corporate trust instrument, professional legal opinion on beneficial ownership, current beneficial-ownership register, declaration from the trust protector or settlor, chain-of-control diagram from the ultimate human beneficial owner to the International Company, and independent KYC forms completed by each material beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a high-risk or non-transparent remitting jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or certified bank statements showing the remitter's legitimate accumulation of funds, audited financial statements or tax returns of the shareholder, executed share subscription or subordinated loan agreement, board minutes approving the capital routing, and a signed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire lacking a proper remittance purpose or using ambiguous narrative text
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution specifying the wire as an equity contribution for software development and cross-border distribution, supporting capital contribution agreement, the bank's completed capital-import declaration or nature-of-funds form, full SWIFT MT103 narrative referencing 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION FOR ISIC 6201 ANTI-CHEAT MIDDLEWARE', and any contractual invoices or term sheets that correspond to the stated purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 to the International Company's dedicated account at the New Zealand receiving bank, using the exact New Zealand bank/branch/account/suffix format where an IBAN is not used. The remitter must include the receiving bank's required purpose-code or nature-of-funds declaration and a compliant narrative such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION FOR CROSS-BORDER ANTI-CHEAT MIDDLEWARE DEVELOPMENT'. The transactional file should include the executed capital contribution resolution, a source-of-funds package, and the bank's standard capital import declaration. Once the MT103 credit is confirmed, the bank will post funds to the escrow or operational account and the treasury officer should preserve the SWIFT FIN message and any MT202 cover payment as the audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service, SaaS, royalty, contractor, and middleware-licence payments, the outbound clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with full remitter and beneficiary details, attested underlying commercial contract, and applicable tax withholding certificate if repayment is for royalty revenue. For physical hardware purchases or contractual supply of development equipment, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit payable at sight, supported by invoices, packing lists, and transport documents. Local New Zealand dollar settlement flows are cleared through the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) and supporting Payments NZ rails, while foreign-currency and cross-border legs clear through the correspondent banking network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) only for a settlement leg in a restricted-convertibility currency, subject to the New Zealand bank's product governance policy
FX swap (rollover) for same-base-currency liquidity management
Cross-currency swap for long-term USD or EUR operating capital with NZD-equivalent liability
Vanilla FX call and put options with physical settlement for contingent royalty and revenue flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the month of the registration anniversary each year; Registrar issues a reminder notice before the due month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 200 (approx. USD 122); failure to file two consecutive annual returns triggers strike-off under s 324 Companies Act 1993, and directors may be fined up to NZD 10,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 7 July following the standard 31 March balance date; extension to 31 March if an approved tax agent files on behalf of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties NZD 250–500 plus use-of-money interest at the prescribed IRD rate; a tax-exempt non-resident entity must file a nil return to maintain its exempt status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST Return (compulsory registration where turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period; optional thereafter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 28th day of the month following the end of each two-monthly or six-monthly GST filing period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Progressive late filing penalties (NZD 50–250 per return) plus late payment interest; zero-rated or exempt offshore software receipts typically produce nil or refundable positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (preparation, and filing where the large-company threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after balance date for companies required to file; small exempt companies must prepare and retain statements at the registered office without filing unless an FMC reporting entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability fines up to NZD 10,000 with court enforcement for non-compliance; audit is compulsory once statutory thresholds are exceeded or shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights demand an audit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is required where the company is an FMC reporting entity, an overseas company required to file financial statements, a large company satisfying at least two of (total assets over NZD 60M, total revenue over NZD 30M, more than 50 full-time employees), or shareholders holding 5% or more of voting rights elect an audit. A small company (assets up to NZD 5.5M, revenue up to NZD 11M, up to 50 employees) is exempt from mandatory audit and from filing financial statements with the Registrar.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand External Reporting Board (XRB) framework: full NZ IFRS (Tier 1) for FMC reporting entities; NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for large non-FMC entities; simplified Tier 3 accounting standards for small for-profit companies. The tax-exempt international company structure prepares nil-basis financial statements under the applicable tier.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand maintains no separate statutory UBO register; the annual return serves as the annual confirmation of directors, registered office, and issued share structure. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members and electronically notified to the Registrar within 10 working days. AML/CFT Act 2009 customer due diligence applies through banking and payment providers (Swift Wire, Stripe), with beneficial ownership reverified on ownership change or on a risk-based refresh cycle.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Cook Islands International Company is treated as a non-resident tax-exempt foreign company; 0% corporate tax on foreign-source income, and no NZ income tax unless it derives New Zealand-source income or becomes NZ tax-resident through management-and-control. NZ resident companies pay 28% on worldwide income. Applicable NZ incentives include the 15% refundable Research & Development Tax Incentive, immediate deduction for low-value assets up to NZ$10,000, and no broad capital gains tax on the realisation of the anti-cheat IP unless the disposal is part of a profit-making undertaking. Imputation credits attach to dividends paid by NZ-resident payers.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit; utilisation requires 49% continuity of beneficial ownership, and 66% continuity is required to carry forward imputation credits)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the Inland Revenue 'myIR' portal or tax-agent approved software (e.g. Xero, MYOB)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July following the end of the income year; terminal tax is due by 7 April following the income year; provisional tax instalments are due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business income from video game anti-cheat engine licensing, SaaS subscriptions, and malware/integrity middleware services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC: include only New Zealand-source income; exclude foreign-source licensing revenue derived outside New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total other income including bank interest, foreign dividends, foreign exchange gains, and capital gains subject to tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude interest or royalties protected by the NZ-Cook Islands DTA where NRWT has already been deducted at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure: R&D wages, cloud infrastructure, third-party software licences, legal, accounting, and marketing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claim deductions only to the extent the expenditure is incurred in deriving New Zealand-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or net loss before tax adjustments; computed as total income less total expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report in NZD; apply New Zealand accounting standards and IRD tax-reconciliation adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: non-deductible entertainment, penalties, depreciation adjustments, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a tax reconciliation note identifying all permanent and temporary differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or assessable loss after applying loss carry-forwards from prior income years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC may use prior-year losses only against the same New Zealand-source business income, subject to continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends received from any NZ-resident subsidiary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC is not entitled to imputation credits on dividends paid by an NZ company unless the shares are held on capital account and treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D Tax Incentive credit claimed on eligible R&D expenditure incurred in New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may claim the credit only if it carries on an R&D activity in New Zealand and meets the approved criteria; attach the RDTI supplementary return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable or refund due after applying RWT, provisional tax paid, foreign tax credits, and NRWT credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty withholding tax credits by attaching the Cook Islands tax residence certificate; refund claims are subject to the 4-year time bar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for a company IR4 filed after the due date, with further monthly penalties up to NZ$250; failure-to-furnish offence fines up to NZ$4,000; use-of-money interest (UOMI) on unpaid terminal tax at the prescribed quarterly rate (approximately 8%-9% p.a. in 2025); shortfall penalties of 20% up to 150% for incorrect returns.
